title: Fourth moment bound by coefficient energy
statement:
Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $F$ be a multilinear coefficient family of degree at most $k$. Suppose $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are independent under $\mu$ and each satisfies the fourth-order invariance moment conditions. Then
\[
\mathbb E_\mu[F(X)^4]\le 9^k\left(\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}F(S)^2\right)^2.
\]
hypotheses_covered: $\mu$ is a probability measure on a measurable space
$F$ is a coefficient family of degree at most $k$
the coordinates of $X$ are independent under $\mu$
each coordinate of $X$ satisfies the fourth-order invariance moment conditions
replaced: Let $F(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}a_S\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ be a real multilinear polynomial of degree at most $k$; let $I_i(F)=\sum_{S\ni i}a_S^2$. Let $(X_i)$ be independent real inputs on a probability space, each measurable up to a null set with finite fourth absolute moment, first three moments $0,1,0$, and fourth moment at most $9$. Then $\mathbb E[F(X)^4]\le9^k(\sum_S a_S^2)^2$.
